text:
dana: Heads-up — I repro'd a mem regression on prod after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Hosts hit OOMs under continuous batching for long-seq workloads.

sasha: Ugh, was that the heuristic that prefers fused-attn kernels when seq_len > 1024?

dana: Yeah. Selector switched to fused_attn_v3 for >1024. Perf looks better latency-wise but packing grows and padding overhead balloons. Seen on 4 different GPUs.

matt: Can you paste the profiler snapshot?

dana: Sure — short excerpt from mem profiler run against a 4xGPU pod:```
AllocSummary:
  total_gpu: 45.6GB
  used_by_model_weights: 29.3GB
  reserved_workspace: 2.0GB
  batching_padding_waste: 5.7GB
  kv_cache_shadowing: 3.2GB
  unaccounted_peak: 5.4GB
```

jess: That batching_padding_waste is huge. Is batch growth because kernel choice increases per-seq temp buffers?

dana: Exactly. Fused kernel allocates an intermediate tile buffer per-seq which we previously amortized; with continuous batching the amortization fails because batch growth pattern changed (more medium-size requests piling up).

oliver: Do we have a quick mitigation? Kernel fallback policy or cap workspace per-invocation?

sasha: We can do two things fast: 1) add a safety cap on per-seq workspace allocation for fused_attn_v3 (soft fail to fused_attn_v2 when sum(workspace) > X), 2) tighten batch growth gating so we don't expand batch if padding delta exceeds threshold.

matt: +1. Also want an allocator tweak: limit slab coalesce for short-lived temp buffers so they don't blow up highwater. That will reduce fragmentation spikes.

dana: I've started a quick patch: selector will compute estimated_workspace = kernel.workspace_per_seq * expected_batch_size and compare against remaining_device_budget. If estimate > 0.15 * free_mem -> fallback. Pushing PR now.

jess: Nice — can you include a telemetry tag to track how often this fallback happens? Need a counter and sample of seq_len distribution.

dana: Will do. Also adding a tiny patch to the continuous-batcher: when growth_predictor sees >30% pad waste projected, it should stop growth and cut to next-scheduling tick.

oliver: Repro steps for QA (from dana):
```bash
# repro config
./run_profiler --env=staging --model=redwood-13b --kernel-selector=auto --workload=continuously_increasing_seq --duration=5m
# then check /tmp/mem-snapshot.json
```

matt: I'll put together a short regression test that simulates the growth pattern and asserts max padding waste < 1GB.

sasha: If the fallback fixes it, we should still plan a follow-up to make fused_attn_v3's tile buffer memory-frugal (reuse across seqs or move to persistent pool).

dana: Filed PERF-4567 for the regression + short-term fallback + telemetry. CI bot attached details below.

ci-bot: Created ticket PERF-4567: "Pad amplification after kernel-selector change -> OOMs under continuous batching". Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PERF-4567 :white_check_mark:

jess: Assigning to @sasha and @dana for the hotfix, @matt for allocator test, @oliver to OWN rollout gating.

oliver: I'll hold the kernel-selector rollout until we see green in staging.

dana: Thanks all — I'll push the PR and request reviews. Ping me if you need reproducer logs. :thumbsup:
